A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mammary carcinogens BaP and PhP can induce DNA damage in the mammary cells and the inflammatory cytokine, IL-6, potentiates this damage via induction of the cytochrome P-450 enzyme, CYP1B, via miR27.
IL-6 is a potent inducer of CYP expression, and CYP expression is required for the genotoxic effect of BaP and the mammary carcinogen PhIP.

the inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6) potentiates the genotoxic effects of dietary carcinogens benza(a) pyrene (BAp) and 2-aminomethyl-6- phenylimidazo [a,b]pyridine (PhIp) via CYP1B expression in mammary cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

IL-6 can selectively potentiate the DNA damaging effects of dietary carcinogens BaP and PhIp in mammary cells via CYP1B-1 expression, and this may contribute to the increased risk of mammary cancer associated with inflammation.
inflammation can increase the genotoxic effects of BaP and other dietary carcinogens in breast cancer.
IL-6 can potentiate the toxicity of dietary carcinogens by inducing CYPs and this mechanism can be exploited to increase the efficacy of BaP and/or PhIP-based chemopreventive strategies.
